content.value_statement: Teams often lose TDD discipline when work spans agents, services, and test levels. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured red-green-refactor workflows, coverage planning, and quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Defines red-green-refactor workflows and TDD readiness checks.
Coordinates unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, and performance testing strategies.
Recommends test suite architecture, test data management, and isolation practices.
Plans TDD metrics such as cycle time, coverage, mutation testing, and quality gates.
Advises on legacy code characterization tests and refactoring safety nets.
Supports testing strategy across Java, C#, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Go.
limitations: Provides guidance and workflow structure; it does not run tests by itself.
Requires project context, framework details, and existing constraints for precise advice.
References an optional implementation playbook that is not included in the scanned package.
Does not replace framework-specific documentation for uncommon tools.

use_cases.title: Plan a new feature with TDD
use_cases.description: Create failing tests, implement minimal code, and define refactor checks before building a feature.

use_cases.title: Protect a legacy refactor
use_cases.description: Build characterization tests, identify seams, and set regression checks before changing old code.

use_cases.title: Standardize team testing practice
use_cases.description: Define quality gates, testing responsibilities, and TDD metrics across services and teams.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tdd-orchestrator to plan a red-green-refactor workflow for [feature]. Include the first failing test, success criteria, and refactor checks.

prompt_templates.title: Map a test strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tdd-orchestrator to map unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end tests for [service]. Identify gaps, owners, and quality gates.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor legacy code safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tdd-orchestrator to create characterization tests for [module] before refactoring. Identify seams, risks, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate multi-agent TDD
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tdd-orchestrator to design a multi-agent TDD workflow for [project]. Assign test responsibilities, quality gates, metrics, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Plan TDD for a payment refund workflow.
output_examples.output: A staged plan with the first failing acceptance test, unit test boundaries, minimal implementation steps, and refactor checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Improve confidence before refactoring a legacy parser.
output_examples.output: A characterization testing approach, dependency seam list, golden master plan, and regression criteria.

output_examples.input: Create quality gates for a microservices test pipeline.
output_examples.output: A testing responsibility map with contract checks, integration boundaries, coverage goals, and feedback loop metrics.

best_practices: Begin each implementation task with an explicit failing test and acceptance criteria.
Keep tests isolated, readable, and mapped to unit, integration, contract, or end-to-end purpose.
Track TDD metrics that drive decisions, such as cycle time, mutation score, and flaky test rate.
anti_patterns: Generating tests after implementation and presenting them as TDD evidence.
Optimizing coverage percentage while ignoring test quality and behavior risk.
Coordinating many agents without ownership, review gates, or shared test standards.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is designed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill write and execute tests?
faq.answer: It gives structured plans, prompts, and review guidance. Test execution still depends on the local project tools.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: The skill references Java, C#, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Go testing workflows.

faq.question: Can it support legacy code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes characterization testing, seam identification, golden master testing, and refactoring safety nets.

faq.question: Is it only for unit testing?
faq.answer: No. It also covers integration, contract, end-to-end, property-based, performance, and mutation testing strategy.

faq.question: How should teams get the best result?
faq.answer: Provide requirements, existing test frameworks, current constraints, and the quality gates the team needs.
